The specification is internally repetitive: the same twenty topic headings recur across six scenario families, with only the final prompt changing. That structure is useful for coverage but dangerous for correctness, because it encourages readers to treat each topic as a self-contained rule rather than as one participant in a shared commit protocol. The most important critique is therefore not whether any single sentence is plausible, but whether the cross-section interactions actually determine committed, rejected, and unknown outcomes.

The recurring crash clause—“after the write but before the acknowledgment”—is the central unresolved boundary. In Sections 1.1 through 1.20, the text repeatedly asks which durable evidence distinguishes
